'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Martin Heinrich]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Martin Heinrich]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNM}} The '''2024 United States Senate election in New Mexico''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[New Mexico]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Martin Heinrich]] won re-election to a third term, defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] financier Nella Domenici. Primary elections took place on June 4, 2024, with both Heinrich and Domenici winning their respective party's nomination unopposed.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Republicans have not won a Senate race in New Mexico since Domenici's late father [[Pete Domenici|Pete]] did so in [[2002 United States Senate election in New Mexico|2002]]. Heinrich was first elected in [[2012 United States Senate election in New Mexico|2012]] by a 5.7-point margin, succeeding longtime Democratic incumbent [[Jeff Bingaman]]. In [[2018 United States Senate election in New Mexico|2018]], Heinrich was reelected to his second term by an overwhelming 23.6-point margin, but this was largely due to the presence of third-party candidate and former [[Governor of New Mexico|governor of the state]] [[Gary Johnson]], who ran as a [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] and garnered over 15% of the vote. Come Election Day in 2024, Heinrich was reelected to a third term in office by 10.12%, receiving 55.1% of the statewide vote to Domenici's 44.9%. While an underperformance of his 2018 margin, his margin of victory was an overperformance of [[Kamala Harris|Kamala Harris']] 6-point victory in the state in the [[2024 United States presidential election in New Mexico|concurrent presidential election]]. Heinrich also held his own quite well at a county-by-county level, particularly when compared to the performances of Kamala Harris. For example, Heinrich carried the counties of [[Guadalupe County, New Mexico|Guadalupe]] and [[Cibola County, New Mexico|Cibola]] by 21.7% and 13.2%, respectively, which Harris carried in the concurrent presidential election by meager margins of 0.72% and 1.6%, respectively. Heinrich also carried [[Socorro County, New Mexico|Socorro County]] by around 4.8%, which was carried by [[Donald Trump]] in the presidential race by around 4%. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates===
